Histological examination of a biopsied SM cyst will reveal thin walls of stratified squamous epithelium without a granular layer, typically with abundant sebaceous input (Figure 2). The cyst is frequently connected to the epidermis by a tissue cord originating from the infundibulum of the pilosebaceous unit [1]. Each steatocystoma is associated with a hair follicle, which can result in retention of trapped vellus hairs in the cystic lumen, as seen in our first patient [1, 2, 7]. panels.rationale: Single-panel Doppler ultrasound from a disease-focused case report ('A Breast Imaging Case of Steatocystoma Multiplex'). The scan is a real patient image of the right breast (1 o'clock position, 3 cm from nipple) showing a circumscribed, avascular, anechoic oil cyst; the in-text and article title attribute these breast oil cysts to the patient's steatocystoma multiplex, so attribution rests on a disease-focused title plus a specific captioned manifestation. The depicted oil cyst matches the vocabulary finding of oily cyst contents; ultrasound-specific features absent from the vocabulary are listed as proposed findings. No age, ethnicity, or skin-tone information is stated, and the image is not a skin photograph, so those fields are null/unknown.

in_text_mentions: The patient’s screening mammogram was performed (Figures 1, 2), and innumerable oil cysts are visualized in both breasts, predominantly in the medial aspect. The patient had a diagnostic mammogram with targeted bilateral breast ultrasound, which showed multiple oval anechoic cystic masses consistent with mammographic findings of multiple oil cysts. A follow-up ultrasound was done (Figure 3), which showed a circumscribed, avascular oil cyst.
